hypothesis: Stack an exact bias-free self-attention QKV projection merge on the retained BF16 linear-attention frontier: concatenate Wq/Wk/Wv in q,k,v row order, execute one BF16 F.linear, and split its output into the original three projections without changing any logical work.

provenance.implementation: Retain SANA_ENABLE_LINATTN_BF16=1 and additionally set SANA_ENABLE_QKV_MERGE=1. Twenty loaded BF16 attention modules build detached [Wq;Wk;Wv] copies and select the single-F.linear branch; compile and cache remain off.

build.note: The higher transformer-load footprint versus Round 3 is consistent with twenty resident detached concatenated QKV weight copies. Build and generation completed with return code 0; the optional DeepGEMM import traceback remained non-fatal.

validity.method_semantics: For bias-free projections, F.linear(x,[Wq;Wk;Wv]).chunk(3,-1) computes q=xWq^T, k=xWk^T, v=xWv^T in the original order. All downstream BF16 aggregation, norms, RoPE, attention, FFN, scheduler, and CFG logic is unchanged.
validity.visual_note: Authenticity-only check passed. All three decoded frame hashes and the MP4 hash exactly match the already inspected valid Round 3 output, while ffprobe independently validates this run's output contract. No output comparison was used as a method correctness gate.

decision.reason: The valid fixed-workload run measures 49.50 seconds, a 1.246x speedup over baseline and a measured 0.22-second/0.44% improvement over Round 3. The margin is small enough to be near run noise, while peak memory rises 726 MiB versus Round 3 because of the merged copies, but it remains 230 MiB below baseline. Retain as the measured latency frontier with the small-margin caveat and continue distinct hypotheses because the 2.5x target is unmet.
